stem.en: A student bags a young pea bud and does not touch its stamens. Will a pod form, and why?

text.en: No, because the bag keeps out every pollen grain

feedback.en: The bag keeps out pollen from outside, but the bud has its own stamens inside.

text.en: Yes, because its own pollen reaches its stigma

feedback.en: Yes. The stamens stay inside the bag and shed pollen onto the stigma.

text.en: No, because a flower in a bud can never form a pod

feedback.en: The bud grows and opens inside the bag. In the activity it formed a pod.

text.en: Yes, because the muslin bag gives the bud its food

feedback.en: A muslin bag gives no food. It only keeps outside pollen away.

explanation.en: The stamens are still inside the bag, so the flower can pollinate itself as it develops. A bag stops pollen from outside. It does not stop the pollen already inside.

hints.en: What is inside the bag along with the stigma?
Does this bud still have its stamens?
